beats.note: Andy Rubin pitched investors in 2004 a camera platform with a cloud portion for storing images online.

beats.name: Andy Rubin and Chris White
beats.role: Founded Android Inc. in Palo Alto in October 2003.

beats.note: Rubin said handsets were the bigger opportunity, and a free operating system could undercut rivals.

beats.text: The same platform became Android for cellphones.
beats.note: 'The exact same platform, the exact same operating system we built for cameras', said in Tokyo on 16 April 2013.

beats.text: The founders joined Google with it.
beats.note: Rubin, Rich Miner, Nick Sears and Chris White all moved across.

beats.name: HTC Dream
beats.role: Sold as the T-Mobile G1, the first commercial Android phone, announced 23 September 2008.

beats.line: The world's biggest phone OS began as a camera OS.
